report.tagline: The world's most used web browser, now with Gemini AI built in to answer questions about pages and do tasks on websites for you.
report.simpleSummary: Chrome is the app you use to open websites on a computer or Android phone. It is free, fast, and saves your passwords, bookmarks and history across devices when you sign in with Google. In 2026 Google added a Gemini side panel that can read the page or your open tabs and answer questions, and 'auto browse', an AI agent that can shop or fill forms for you. Chrome makes money for Google mostly by sending your searches to Google Search, where ads are shown.

overview.whatItDoes: Chrome is a free browser for Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, iPhone and Chromebooks. It loads websites, runs web apps like Gmail and Google Docs, and syncs data across devices. Its address bar is also a Google search box, which is its main business purpose. Gemini in Chrome adds AI help and agent tasks.
howItWorks: Users type in the address bar; anything that is not a web address becomes a Google search.
Signing in syncs passwords, bookmarks, tabs and history across devices.
Extensions from the Chrome Web Store add features like ad blockers or grammar tools.
The Gemini side panel reads the current page or a group of tabs and answers questions.
Auto browse can complete multi-step tasks like buying an item, pausing for the user on logins and final payment.
Chrome updates itself every few weeks in the background, with security fixes.
overview.valueProposition: A fast, safe, free browser that works the same on every device, with Google services and now AI help built in.

businessModel.summary: Chrome is free. It makes money for Google indirectly: it sends searches to Google, keeps users signed in to Google services, and now sells AI subscriptions. Google also uses Chrome to make sure no other company controls how people reach the web.

revenueStreams.detail: Searches from the address bar go to Google Search, which earns from ads.
Advanced Gemini features like auto browse need Google AI Pro or Ultra.
Paid security and management for companies.
Licence fees from laptops running ChromeOS.

businessModel.pricing: Chrome is free. Google AI Pro costs about $20 a month in the US (about ₹1,950 in India); Ultra costs about $250 a month in the US. Chrome Enterprise Premium has per-user pricing.
businessModel.unitEconomics: A typical Chrome user might make 2 to 3 searches a day from the address bar. If Google earns, say, ₹1 to ₹2 per search in ad revenue in India, and more in the US, one user is worth a few hundred to a thousand rupees a year. Running Chrome for one more user costs almost nothing. AI features change that: each Gemini answer and auto browse task costs real computing money, so Google gates heavier tasks behind paid AI plans.

howTheyGetUsers: Promoted on Google.com and YouTube to people on other browsers
Default on Chromebooks used in schools
Word of mouth about speed and sync
whatBringsUsersBack: Habit: it is the default way to open the web
growth.moat: Chrome's moat is habit and data lock-in: your passwords, history and extensions are all there, and it is the default on Android. Most rival browsers, including Atlas and Comet, are built on Chromium, Google's own open-source engine, so Google still shapes the web platform. The new risk is that AI agents make the browser less important than the assistant inside it.

pmLessons: A free product can be worth billions if it protects your main business, like Chrome sending searches to Google.
Leaders must respond quickly when a new kind of product appears, as Chrome did with Gemini after AI browsers launched.
Lock-in through saved data is powerful, but only if the product keeps up.
Agents need trust: users must see and control what the AI does on their behalf.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Chrome respond to ChatGPT Atlas?
interviewQuestions.hint: Who is switching, why, what Chrome does better (sync, scale), what it lacks. Plan: free AI features, agent trust, metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of auto browse?
interviewQuestions.hint: Adoption, completion rate, time saved, repeat use, errors. Guardrails on payments.

interviewQuestions.question: Chrome memory complaints are rising. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment by device and tab count, find top causes (extensions, sites), fix with tab sleeping and limits.

interviewQuestions.question: Why does Google invest so much in a free browser?
interviewQuestions.hint: Distribution for Search, control of web standards, data and AI. Show the money flow.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a Chrome feature for students.
interviewQuestions.hint: Persona, tasks (research, notes), Gemini summaries and citations, focus mode. Metric: weekly study sessions.
